title: Pineapple Sweet & Sour Sauce
description: Pineapple juice and apricot preserves bring sweetness and shine to a red takeout sauce sharpened with rice vinegar.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tsp total.

steps.title: Dissolve the preserves
steps.text: Warm {pi}, {w} and {ap} over medium heat for 3 minutes, whisking until smooth.

steps.title: Balance the fruit
steps.text: Whisk in {rv}, {to} and {a}. Let the sauce bubble gently for 3 minutes until the tomato is fully blended into the juice.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over sauced pork medallions, or pour into a warm bowl for dipping soft chicken pieces.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/2 tsp coconut aminos in place of 3 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace half the pineapple juice with water and reduce the vinegar to 1 teaspoon. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 62 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 15.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 75 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 59 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 14.6 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 19 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
